key_insight: Rectified-flow generation paired with exact latent-space refinement enables concurrent design of printable bone-scaffold microstructures and their spatial assignments to meet mechanical targets.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports porous, mechanically matched implants by jointly optimizing scaffold architecture across microstructural and anatomical scales.
method: Generate periodic lattice cells with a conditional rectified-flow model.
Refine cells in latent space using exact finite-element homogenization sensitivities.
Jointly optimize cell geometries and spatial assignments under mechanical and feature-size constraints.
evidence_signal: Computational benchmarks report under 1% error across six target moduli for all eight rabbit flow-started refinements, plus human scaffolds with 63% cortical porosity and compliance within 2%, and 84% cancellous porosity with strain-energy deviations below 0.25%.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational performance but does not establish fabricated-scaffold validation, manufacturing robustness, or biological outcomes.
paper_title: Concurrent two-scale topology optimization of printable bone scaffolds via rectified-flow generation and exact latent-space refinement
